name: What is the difference between a general contractor and a specialty subcontractor?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a general contractor and a specialty subcontractor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A general contractor oversees the entire job from rough framing to final punch lists, while a specialty subcontractor handles one specific trade, such as electrical or plumbing. On a major renovation, choosing a general contractor eliminates the burden of scheduling separate vendors yourself. The general contractor acts as the primary contact on-site, supervising daily progress, performing hands-on work like custom framing and finish carpentry, and coordinating licensed sub-trades to ensure mechanical installations integrate cleanly with drywall, tile, and paint.
acceptedAnswer.description: A general contractor oversees the entire project, timeline, and all trades. A subcontractor focuses strictly on a single trade, such as licensed plumbing or electrical work.
